rail.label: 19–20 Sep
rail.title: SingHacks: the prototype
rail.summary: The prototype that took us to the finals: one web page, synthetic sources, and a language model choosing what to buy.
bullets: A research desk that bought synthetic premium sources within an XRP budget and wrote a cited dossier.
A language model planned each purchase; payment was a fixture by default, with optional Testnet settlement.
The frozen prototype held 34 files and 970 lines of code (tag hackathon-baseline).

image.alt: The SingHacks prototype: a verified dossier page with supporting and challenging evidence
image.caption: Prototype dossier, from the hackathon-baseline tag

rail.label: 5 Oct
rail.title: First payment on the XRPL Testnet
rail.summary: Writers were paid at their own Testnet wallets, and the run showed the ledger entry.
bullets: Each writer gets its own Testnet wallet and is paid there directly.
The run shows the ledger transaction instead of a simulated receipt.
Testnet money has no real value; that label has stayed on every surface since.

image.alt: The October app: a question box with a budget and suggested questions
image.caption: The app in early October

rail.label: 8 Oct
rail.title: Code decides what to buy, inside your budget
rail.summary: Purchases moved from the language model to deterministic policy code, inside a budget set once.
bullets: A neutral search across every listed writer instead of an allowlist of sites.
A decision model scores each article; only policy code can make the purchase.
A five-second plan card confirms the plan; no pop-up interrupts each purchase.

image.alt: The app on 9 October with a budget picker and suggested questions
image.caption: The app on 9 October

rail.label: 10 Oct
rail.title: AI Tinkerers Singapore talk
rail.summary: An on-stage demo of the October build for AI Tinkerers Singapore, a separate chapter from the finals.
bullets: The refund story on stage: a bought article breaks its promise and the money comes back.
The October build log, replayed from git and the coding agents' logs, is kept as an archive.
The talk deck and speaker notes stay on this site.

image.alt: The ResearchAgent demo on stage at AI Tinkerers Singapore
image.caption: On stage, 10 October

rail.label: 3 Nov
rail.title: Any agent can search and buy
bullets: MCP server: search writers and buy within human-set caps, four stdio tools.
Nightly scorecard and a six-rule read-only hard-gate audit.
Builder feedback (15 findings), MIT licence, contributing and security policy.

rail.title: The app, done properly
bullets: Keyboard-first Run and Writers views, brand kit and exports.

rail.label: 3 Nov
rail.title: Fact menu
bullets: Signed fact menus in decisions. Live selection F1 0.235 → 0.419; wasted spend regressed 36.2% → 47.2%; the follow-up is #276.
Typed SDK, shared MCP client and architecture seams.
Startup-style README and one header across the explainers site.

image.caption: Decisions panel with the fact menu

rail.label: 3 Nov
rail.title: Mac app
bullets: Offline Electron app, DMG and Keychain storage; installed launch to interactive 2.088 s (single local sample).
Hire the agent over x402; continuous payment recovery; publish Markdown folders as paid Testnet writers.

image.alt: The installed Mac app showing a completed answer
image.caption: Installed Mac app, from the v0.4.0 release assets

rail.label: 3 Nov
rail.title: The money, made clear
bullets: Shell, plan, payments, refund and net Spend UI; four allowed keyframes.
Wasted-purchase analysis and a frozen 140-question evaluation with confidence intervals.
Proof-or-refund XRPL escrow with durable buyer cancellation; tamper-evident audit trail and `COMPLIANCE.md`.

image.alt: A run in progress: the payments rail shows a purchase being made within the budget
image.caption: Buying, with spend shown against the budget

rail.label: 3 Nov
rail.title: Answers, made clear
bullets: Answer and claims redesign; the UC3 PDF went from 50 to 4 pages.
Value-of-information veto in the decision policy; held-out waste 39.39% → 35.48% (target missed).
Scoped allowance per agent from one wallet.

image.alt: A finished answer with the lead finding, one refunded and one verified purchase
image.caption: Finished answer: one kept, one refunded

rail.label: 3 Nov
rail.title: Proof you can check
bullets: `npm run verify:answer` checks an exported answer: 40/40 citations and 4/4 Testnet checks in the recorded run; a tampered file exits 1.
Payment chaos testing: 1,729 fault episodes, 431 SIGKILLs, zero double charges (fixture only).
Refreshed README and shared site header.

rail.label: 3 Nov
rail.title: Any agent, one wallet
bullets: SDK v1: typed streaming asks, verification and journaled x402 payments.
Mac app hosts MCP over loopback HTTP with per-agent Keychain tokens and allowances, plus `verify_answer` and `hire` tools.
Crash-safe engine restart, notify-only update checks, separate arm64 and x64 DMGs (unsigned).

image.alt: Settings page: connect an agent with its own capped allowance
image.caption: Connect an agent with its own allowance (Settings, captured 7 Nov)

rail.label: 4 Nov
rail.title: Fair exchange: the writer is paid by publishing the key
bullets: Release-candidate SDK, Python and MCP artifacts; desktop CI downloads Electron before DMG builds.
Key-reveal escrow on first touch and in the live Testnet product.
Fix Testnet reachability and first-impression money consistency.

image.alt: A finished Testnet run: escrow created, writer published the key, the hash matches, the article decrypts
image.caption: Key-reveal run on Testnet (captured 7 Nov)

rail.label: 5 Nov
rail.title: Real Testnet without cloning the repo
bullets: Zero-clone Testnet MCP and app, fixture models, fictional writers and no real value; writer onboarding and judge path.
TEST-SGD IOU key-reveal token escrow: three happy paths and a no-show cancellation; stand-in for RLUSD, not real RLUSD.
RC.2 artifacts and generated installs; completed answers poll for their validated anchor without reload (browser regression).

image.alt: The zero-clone Testnet app with an audited budget change
image.caption: Zero-clone Testnet app, budget change audited (captured 7 Nov)

rail.label: 7 Nov
rail.title: One command to a verified purchase
bullets: Opt-in TEST-SGD key-reveal token escrow on the zero-clone MCP and app with `--testnet --iou`.
One-shot `try --testnet` judge path: UC3 with a S$2 cap, six numbered ledger links, `--ledger` verification and `RESULT PASS`.
Stranger writer onboarding: `init <dir>` scaffolds two commented example notes.

rail.label: 7 Nov
rail.title: Answers lead with the fact you paid for
bullets: Anchored abstentions: a DONE Testnet run that buys nothing now carries the 12-drop audit anchor, so every DONE Testnet run verifies online.
22 sourced XRPL explainers from a disclosed "team-authored explainer · sources cited · not an independent writer · Testnet" writer.
Blind judge banks: v3 held-out, dev and negatives.

image.alt: An answer whose first sentence is the purchased fact, with its citation
image.caption: Answer-first layout (captured 7 Nov)

rail.label: 8 Nov
rail.title: Honest states for anchors and no-purchase runs
bullets: Anchor pending is no longer a failure.
Anchored no-purchase runs show "Anchored on XRPL · no purchase · ledger N" and the Export menu; simulated declines stay "not anchored (simulated)".
The plan modal and home subtitle state the real rule.

misses.did: Kept the timeouts beside the passes; the 90 s limit stayed unchanged.
misses.measure: 2 of 4 cold runs over 90 s: 73.8 s pass · 90.2 s timed out · stopped at the 90 s deadline · 84.2 s pass

misses.title: Most blind held-out questions did not end in a purchase
misses.did: Reported the blind number instead of the dev bank, and froze a new blind bank (v5).
misses.measure: 13 of 20 held-out questions ended without a cited purchase; the key fact led the answer in 2 of 20

misses.title: We replaced our own better-looking number
misses.did: The v2 held-out score was written after the team notes; a blind v4 bank replaced it everywhere.

misses.title: The loaded-host soak failed its loop-delay gate
misses.did: Kept the failure; a quiet-host rerun passed all five gates. No threshold changed.
misses.measure: Loop delay p99 64.4 ms against a 50 ms limit on a busy host; 25.8 ms when quiet

misses.title: First stablecoin-escrow start was slow

misses.measure: 122.9 s cold against a 100 s target; 21.5 s warm

misses.title: No buy threshold met the waste ceiling
